Govt. of Nct of Delhi Through the Secretary (Power) Vikas Bhawan New Delhi 2. Bses Rajdhani Power Ltd. Through Chief Executive Delhi Secretariat 5th Floor, I.P. Estate New Delhi. Also at: Bses Bhawan Nehru Place, New Delhi. 3. Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. 3rd Floor, Maker Chambers, 4, Nariman Point, Mumbai-400021. 4. M/s D.S. Construction Limited A-97-98, Lajpat Nagar-I New Delhi.
texts.facts: Brief facts of the case, relevant for the disposal of the present suit are that the plaintiff has filed the present suit seeking compensation for Rs.10,00,000/- from the defendants. Plaintiff submits that defendant no.1 is responsible for over all supervision and control on production, storage and transmission of electricity in Delhi and defendant no.2 has become the successor of Delhi Vidyut Board in respect of the responsibility, control and management of transmission of electricity and responsible for maintenance, control and transfer of electricity including one where the cause of action for filing the present suit arose. 2. It is averred that plaintiff is working as Project Engineer with A2Z Engineering & Maintenance Services Limited at Karnal Haryana and is getting salary of Rs.11,250/- per month and is only son of his parents. Plaintiff got his very first job with defendant no.2 as GIS Engineer in July 2008 with a salary of Rs.9,000/- per month. On 18.11.2009 plaintiff changed his service from BSES to A2Z Engineering & Maintenance Services Limited at Karnal Haryana as a Project Engineer with a salary of Rs.9,000/- per month + HRS and mobile phone facility. In April, 2010 his salary was increased @ Rs.11,250/- per month in place of Rs.9,000/-. On 21.03.2010 after his duty plaintiff boarded in bus coming to Delhi for picking-up his goods from his friend Mr. Somesh Shah who was residing at Sec. 27, Noida. Plaintiff took auto-rickshaw bearing no.DL1RK-3884 from Kashmiri Gate Bus Station and reached at the Red Light Signal Opposite Mayur Vihar Phase-I, Metro Station, Delhi-Noida Link Road, Mayur Vihar Phase-I, Delhi. In the meantime, suddenly an Electric Pole of High Tension wire fell on the Auto-Rikshaw bearing no.DL1RK-3884 in which the plaintiff was traveling and due to said accident, auto-rickshaw got badly damaged and burnt as electricity was passing through the High Tension Wire. The severity of the said accident is res ipsa loquitor from the fact that the auto driver Sh. Ashok Kumar died on the spot due to the said accident and plaintiff sustained serious injuries on his face, head and all over his body and became unconscious. He was taken to Jeevan Anmol Hospital by one Col. Manoj and admitted there vide MLC no. 743 dt. 22.03.2010. A FIR bearing no. 107/2010 was registered at PS Pandav Nagar. It is further averred that apart from serious and grievous injuries on his face and head, plaintiff sustained multiple fractures on his face and head and several injuries on his left knee, left forearm, left index finger. After examination, the doctors detected that plaintiff has sustained 14 fractures as well as other injuries due to the said accident. It is further averred that plaintiff was operated and remained admitted for treatment from 22.03.2020 to 01.04.2010. During operation, the plates have been inserted in forehead and jaw of the plaintiff and 62 stitches has been given to the plaintiff from forehead to eye and 65 stitches at nose and left knee and was on complete bed rest upto 21.05.2010. On 22.05.2010 the plaintiff joined his duty however, since the condition of the plaintiff was further deteriorated, the plaintiff was again advised to take complete bed rest from 26.05.2010 to 22.06.2010. Due to the unfortunate accident, engagement ceremony fixed for 05.04.2010 could not be performed and was cancelled considering the serious condition of the plaintiff. 3. Plaintiff further avers that the said accident was caused due to the negligent acts of the defendant no.2 who was responsible to take care and maintain its high tension wires and poles containing the said wires. Had the defendant no.2 taken care of the poles the aforesaid accident could not happened. The fall of the poles shows that the same was not properly fixed in the earth and was not inspected or checked by the defendant no.2. The defendant no.1 is also responsible for the acts of the defendant no.2 and is thus arrayed in the present suit. The defendant no.3 and 4 are the insurance Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/ 2 company of the defendant no.2 and are under obligation to compensate the person who suffered due to the negligent act of the defendant no.2 and therefore, all the defendants are jointly and severally liable to compensate the plaintiff. 4. Plaintiff incurred expenditure on treatment about Rs.3 lacs for hospitalization, operation, medicines, Rs.1 lac approx on his extra nutrition and betterment, Rs.1 lac on taxies/ambulance and hotels. Plaintiff remained absent from his duty w.e.f. 21.03.2010 to 21.05.2010 and also from 26.05.2010 to 22.06.2010 and the said loss comes to Rs.33,750/-. Due to the said accident, plaintiff's future has been shattered and even today, plaintiff is not working well as he is suffering pain and feels that there are two images of the one things. The plaintiff is accessing his loss toward physical pain, mental pain, suffering, future loss, loss of companion, loss of wages etc. @ Rs.4,66,250/-. It is further averred that no money can compensate the plaintiff towards the losses suffered by the plaintiff due to the said accident, however, plaintiff is restricting himself and is claiming a compensation of Rs.10 lacs against all the defendants. Hence, plaintiff has filed the present suit for compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- in his favour and against the defendants with 24% per annum interest thereon till date of actual payment. 5. As per record, the defendant no.1 has been proceeded exparte vide order dt. 20.09.2011 and there is no written statement of defendant no.1 on record. 6. Written statement was filed by defendant no.2 wherein it is stated that on 21.03.2010 the report of the accident was prepared and it was found that M/s D.S. Construction Limited was carrying out the work of road widening and the fly over on Delhi-Noida Link Road opposite to Delhi Police Apartment. The company while carrying out the work had indulged in heavy excavation or a hit to the tower by the heavy machinery. The competent authority of Government of NCT of Delhi vide its letter dt. 31.03.2010 had also constituted an enquiry committee to see whether there is any negligence on the part of any agency. The said committee had given an interim report dt. 07.04.2010 and final report dt. 28.08.2010. In the final report, it was specifically held that, "responsibility cannot be fixed to any known person or agency as the reason of collapse of towers is due to mischievous act of unknown persons.". It is averred that answering defendant carries out the routine checkups of inter alia its high tension towers and whenever any of its part including fish plates are missing, a report is also lodged with the police. In this case no police complaint was ever lodged as till the last of such inspections which was carried out periodically no fish plates were missing. The site inspections are carried out regularly and is also recorded and the last checkup was carried out in March 2010 only. 7. Defendant no.3 also filed its written statement wherein it has been submitted that answering defendant is liable to indemnify only that loss which is admitted by M/s BSES YPL subject to insurance policy is effective on claims made basis which was effective for the period 19.12.2012 to 18.12.2013 therefore, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. is not liable to indemnify any loss to insured and to pay compensation to plaintiff and answering defendant be deleted from the array of respondents. It is averred that answering defendant is having the policy contract with M/s BSES YPL and is not a direct party in relation to the claimant. The liability of the answering defendant will be Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/ 3 devalued if the negligence of BSES is proved. There is no cause of action against the answering defendant as BSES has not intimated about the happening of the alleged accident as per terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy. Thus, it is prayed that answering defendant be deleted from the array of defendants and suit of the plaintiff be dismissed with heavy cost as the same is bad for misjoinder and non- joinder of necessary and proper parties. 8. Vide order dated 20.09.2011, the original defendant no.3 & 4 i.e. Reliance General Insurance Company and Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. were deleted from array of parties. Subsequently, on 13.02.2018 defendant no.3 Reliance General Insurance Company and defendant no.4 M/s D.S. Construction were impleaded in the present suit 9. Plaintiff further examined H.C. Vinay Bhargav as PW-2 who proved the registration of FIR Ex.PW1/8. 15. Plaintiff also examined Sh. Irfan Ali, Medical Record Officer from Jeevan Anmol Hospital who proved the medical examination of plaintiff was conducted from 22.03.2010 to 01.04.2010. He got exhibited the medical documents of plaintiff as Ex.PW3/A (running into sixty one pages). 16. Plaintiff's witnesses were duly cross-examined on behalf of defendant no.2, defendant no.3 and defendant no.4 respectively. Thereafter, plaintiff's evidence was closed vide order dt. 26.02.2020. Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/ 6 17. Defendant no.2 examined Sh. R.K. Tola, Ex.-GM(T), Delhi Transco Limited as D2W1 who proved the inquiry report dt. 07.04.2010 and final report dt. 28.08.2010 Mark D2W1/A and Mark D2W1/B. 18. Defendant no.3 i.e. M/s Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. examined Sh. Dharmender Singh, Admn. Manager, as D3W1. He got exhibited his identity card as Ex.D3W1/1. He proved the attested true copy of insurance policy as Ex.D3W1/2. In his cross-examination he submitted that defendant no.2 was insured with defendant no.3 and alleged policy was valid for the period of 19.12.2009 to 18.12.2010. As per the terms and conditions and contract of insurance between the defendant no.2 & 3, defendant no.3 is liable to pay compensation/liability to BSES YPL, if there is no violation of terms and condition and contract of insurance. He admitted that, 'our contract is with defendant no.2'. Thereafter, Ld. Counsel for defendant no.3 closed evidence on behalf of defendant no.3 on 30.05.2023. 19. Defendant no.4 examined Sh. Santosh Kumar Gupta as D4W1 who proved the board resolution dt. 03.10.2017 as Mark D4W1/1 (Ex.D4W1/1) and board resolution dt. 20.03.2023 as Ex.D4W1/2. In his cross-examination witness deposed that during the relevant period defendant no.4 company was executing the work of flyover, bridges etc. defendant no.4 company was not executing any work near the place of accident and we had taken all safety measures for construction work. He deposed that he was coordinating for the PWD work awarded to defendant no.4 company and was visiting site from time to time. But at the time of accident, he was not present. He denied that accident took place due to negligence of defendant no.4 company. Thereafter, evidence on behalf of defendant no.4 company was closed matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: It is further averred that there is compulsory excess clause i.e. Rs.1 lac for each and every claim. It has been submitted by answering defendant that the reason for accident was either the heavy excavation or a hit to the lower by the heavy machinery therefore, no cause of action has arisen against M/s BSES YPL and answering defendant. Defendant no.4 also filed its written statement thereby therein that no relief was claimed by the plaintiff against the defendant no.4 in its original plaint and it was only on the basis of the allegations raised by the defendant no.2 in its written statement, that the defendant no.4 was carrying out the works of road widening, the defendant no.4 was arrayed as a party to the proceedings. It is further stated that averments contained in the written statement qua the defendant no.4 are extremely vague and misconceived as any accident/mis-happening or loss/damage to any person/property which may be arising due to any electricity pole shall be solely of the defendant no.2 whereas pleading shows that defendant no.2 has sought to shift its liability to defendant no.4 which is vague and unsubstantiated. The entire basis of the allegation is a self styled report dated 22.03.2010 made by defendant no.2 which was allegedly forwarded to the Chief Electrical Inspector, Government of NCT of Delhi. The said report neither has any basis nor any supporting document to even remotely suggest as to how the defendant no.4 is sought to be made liable for the alleged accident. It has been further submitted that it was the duty of the defendant no.2 to ensure that the poles are properly embedded as the same are stacked in an open public area. It was certainly the duty of the defendant no.2 to ensure that any of their acts to not cause any harm or injury to any other person. Defendant no.2 was negligent in not taking appropriate safety measures even after being well aware of the fact that the electric poles were kept stacked in public place, where general public had easy access. Thus, the liability if any, should be attributed to the defendant no.2 for breach of duty for maintaining the electric poles, leading to the alleged accident. It has been further submitted that the allegation of the plaintiff that the answering defendant was negligent in carrying out the work of road widening the flyover is wholly false and baseless. The answering defendant duly carried out the requisite inspection and checks, and completed the entire project with utmost care and caution and there has been no act on the part of answering defendant which has lead to any hard to the plaintiff as alleged. Thus, it has been prayed that the present suit be dismissed with heavy costs on the plaintiff. 10. Replication to the written statement of defendant no.2 filed on behalf of plaintiff thereby reiterating and reaffirming the contents of his plaint. Plaintiff averred that defendant no.2 is trying to shift its liability on M/s D.S. Constructions Limited and defendant no.2 be directed to furnish the complete details of M/s D.S. Constructions Limited so that the plaintiff can take necessary action of impleading M/s D.S. Constructions Limited as defendant in the present suit. Plaintiff denied the final report and stated that it is the defendant no.2 who was negligent in regular monitoring of its electrical towers and poles. Rest of the contents of the written statement are denied by the plaintiff. Plaintiff averred that initially the plaintiff has not incorporated the answering defendant in the array of parties as at that time the plaintiff was unaware about the fact that the answering defendant was doing widening of road and due to the negligent act of the answering defendant, the high tension wire collapsed and the plaintiff sustained grievous injuries. It is further averred that answering defendant intentionally and deliberately trying to shift its liability on the defendant no.2. Presence of answering defendant is duly proved as he is specifically stated under para that, "the defendant no.4 carrying out road widening activities in the said area", but deliberately denying its liability and negligent act. It is submitted that the defendant no.4 has already been incorporated in the array of parties and the plaintiff has already filed amended memo of parties on record. It is averred that defendant no.2 and defendant no.4 both are shifting their burden against each other. In fact the accident has been caused due to the negligent act of the defendant no.2 and 4 and defendant no.3 being insurer of defendant no.2 is liable to pay damages to the plaintiff. 22.2 During the arguments, Ld. Counsel for defendant no.4 drew the attention of this Court towards the report of committee wherein clause 8.2, it is mentioned that, 'BSES has put the blame on PWD and movement of their heavy machinery in road widening work as cause of collapsing of towers. BSES could not produced structural design and drawing of towers due to the fact that these were done originally by DVB nearly 20-25 years back and are not available to them. Ld. Counsel for defendant Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/ 7 no.4 further argued that the report of committee has nowhere given any finding against the defendant no.4. 22.3 As far as the contention of Ld. Counsel for defendant no.2 that it was the duty of defendant no.4 to follow the safety norms of electricity rules is concerned, suffice is to say that the defendant no.2 is/was under the duty to get compliance of the said rules from the defendant no.4 which defendant no.2 failed to do so. 22.4 Moreover during cross-examination by Ld. Counsel for defendant no.2, PW1 deposed that, 'I cannot say whether the cause of calling of high tension tower on 21.03.2010 was due to work of road widening carried out by defendant no.4 DSC Limited or due to heavy excavation work which was done by using heavy machinery, equipments, by defendant no.4 or the cause of accident was negligence of defnedant no.2. 23.4 In the written statement, the defendants has simplicitor denied the contention in the plaint mentioning that there was no negligence of the defendants. At this stage it is relevant to impute strict liability upon the defendants as the doctrine of strict liability has its origin in English Common Law when it was propounded in the celebrated case of Rylands v. Fletcher, 1868 Law Reporter (3) HL330. The rule of strict liability was approved and followed in India in several decisions and has been reiterated in the catena of judgments. The sum and substance of this principle is that due to the action or inaction of the State or its officers, the fundamental rights of a citizen are infringed then the liability of the State, its officials and its instrumental also is strict. Claims raised for compensation in such a case is not a private law claim of damages, under which the damages recoverable are large. Claim made for compensation in public law for compensating the claimants for deprivation of life and public liberty which has nothing to do Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/ 10 with a claim in a private law claim in tort in ordinary civil suit. Even if all the safety measures had been adopted, a person undertaking an activity involving hazardous or risky exposure to human life is liable under law of torts to compensate for the injury suffered by any other person, irrespective of any negligence or carelessness on the part of the Managers of such undertaking. The basis of such liability is the foreseeable risk inherent in the very nature of such activity. The liability cast on such person is known in law as strict liability and it differs from the liability which arise on account of negligence i.e. the concept of negligence comprehends that the foreseeable harm could be avoided by taking reasonable precautions . 27. It may be noted that though not quoted, reliance is placed on M.P. Electricity Board v. Shail Kumari (2002) 2 SCC 162 and Union of India v. Prabhakaran Vijay Kumar (2008) 9 SCC 527,wherein, it was reiterated that the rule of strict liability as laid down byHon'ble Supreme Court in M.C. Mehta Case (1987) 1 SCC 395 is not subject to any exceptions as laid down in the judgment of Rylands v. Flethcher (supra) and in Shail Kumar (supra) it has been observed in para no. 8 & 12 as under : "8. Even assuming that all such measures have been adopted, a person undertaking an activity involving hazardous or risky exposure to human life, is liable under law of torts to compensate for the injury suffered by any other person, irrespective of any negligence or carelessness on the part of the managers of such undertakings. The liability cast on such person is known, in law, as "strict liability". It differs from the liability which arises on account of the negligence or fault in this way i.e. the concept of negligence comprehends that the foreseeable harm could be avoided by taking reasonable precautions. If the defendant did all that which could be done for avoiding the harm he cannot be held liable when the action is based on any negligence attributed. But such consideration is not relevant in cases of strict liability where the defendant is held liable irrespective of whether he could have avoided the particular harm by taking precautions......xxxxx 12. In M.C. Mehta v. Union of India this Court has gone even beyond the rule of strict liability by holding that "where an enterprise is engaged in a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity and harm is caused on any one on account of the accident in the operation of such activity, the enterprise is strictly and absolutely liable to compensate those who are affected by the accident; such liability is not subject to any of the exceptions to the principle of strict liability under the rule in Rylands v. Fletcher." 28. Applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur and strict liability, it was not for the plaintiffs to prove that the defendants were negligent rather it was the defendants to prove that defendants were not negligent and has taken every precaution for safety of all. The factum of accident of plaintiff on account of fall of high tension tower as a result of negligence of defendant no.2 is proved, the negligence is the breach of the duty caused by omission to do something which a reasonable man, guided by those considerations, which ordinary regulates the conduct of human affairs would do or Ajay Kumar vs State on 6 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35976961/ 11 doing something which a prudent or reasonable man would not do. 29. It is proved that the responsibility of the maintenance and upkeep of the towers at the accident site was upon the defendant no.2. The primary liability to compensate the sufferer is that of a supplier of electricity authorities manning such dangerous commodities, who has extra duty to chalk out measures to prevent such major mishappening. Even assuming that all such measures have been adopted, a person undertaking an activity involving hazardous or risky exposure to human life is liable under law of torts to compensate for the injuries suffered by any other person, irrespective or any negligence or carelessness on the part of the managers of such undertakings. The liability cast on such person is known in law as strict liability, it differs from liability which arises on account of negligence i.e. the concept of negligence comprehends that the force in a harm can be avoided by taking reasonable precaution. 33. The liability cast on such person is known in law as strict liability, it differs from liability which arises on account of negligence i.e. the concept of negligence comprehends that the force in a harm can be avoided by taking reasonable precaution.
